content: Ciclesonide nasal spray is prescribed to treat symptoms of both seasonal allergic rhinitis (which occurs at specific times of the year) and perennial allergic rhinitis (which occurs year-round). These symptoms include sneezing, nasal congestion, runny nose, and nasal itching. Ciclesonide belongs to a class of medications known as corticosteroids. It works by reducing and preventing inflammation in the nasal passages, which helps alleviate these symptoms. Ciclesonide nasal spray is available as a liquid solution that is sprayed into the nose. It is typically used once daily, with one spray in each nostril. It is important to use the medication at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed; do not use more or less than prescribed, and do not use it more frequently than instructed. This medication is intended for nasal use only. Do not swallow the spray, and avoid spraying it into your eyes or directly onto the nasal septum (the wall between the nostrils). Ciclesonide helps control the symptoms of rhinitis but does not cure the condition. You may not notice improvement in your symptoms for at least 24 to 48 hours after starting the medication, and it may take longer to experience the full benefits. Continue using the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. Each bottle of ciclesonide nasal spray is designed to provide 120 sprays after it is initially primed. The bottle should be discarded after 4 months of use. To keep track, count 4 months from the date the bottle is removed from its foil pouch and write this date on the provided sticker. Place the sticker on the bottle as a reminder. Additionally, keep track of the number of sprays used, and discard the bottle after 120 sprays, even if there is liquid remaining and it has not yet been 4 months. To use the nasal spray, follow these steps: 1. Gently shake the bottle and remove the dust cover. 2. If using the pump for the first time, point the bottle away from your body and press down and release the pump eight times. If the pump has not been used in the last 4 days, press down and release it once or until a fine spray appears. 3. Clear your nostrils by blowing your nose. 4. Close one nostril with your finger. 5. Hold the bottle upright with your forefinger and middle finger on either side of the spray tip and your thumb supporting the base. 6. Tilt your head slightly forward and carefully insert the spray tip into your open nostril. 7. Begin to breathe in through your nose, and while inhaling, press down quickly and firmly on the applicator to release a spray. 8. Repeat steps 4–7 for the other nostril unless your doctor advises otherwise. 9. Wipe the applicator tip with a clean tissue and replace the dust cover. Ciclesonide may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using ciclesonide nasal spray, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ciclesonide, other nasal corticosteroids (e.g., beclomethasone, budesonide, fluticasone, mometasone, triamcinolone), or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or have recently taken. Mention medications such as ketoconazole or oral steroids (e.g., dexamethasone, methylprednisolone, prednisone), as your doctor may need to adjust your doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had tuberculosis, cataracts, glaucoma, untreated infections, nasal sores, or herpes infections of the eye. Also, let your doctor know if you have recently had nasal surgery or an injury to your nose. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using ciclesonide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform the healthcare provider that you are using ciclesonide. If you have been taking oral steroids, your doctor may gradually reduce your steroid dose after starting ciclesonide. During this transition, your body may take time to adjust, and you may experience symptoms such as extreme fatigue, muscle weakness, stomach pain, loss of appetite, weight loss, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, fainting, depression, irritability, or skin darkening. Inform your doctor if these symptoms occur. Ciclesonide may reduce your ability to fight infections. Avoid contact with sick individuals and wash your hands frequently. Stay away from people with chickenpox or measles, and inform your doctor immediately if you are exposed to these viruses. Unless directed otherwise by your doctor, continue your normal diet. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ciclesonide may cause side effects. Common side effects include headache, nosebleeds, nasal burning or irritation, and earache. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include painful white patches in the nose or throat, flu-like symptoms, vision problems, nasal injuries, new or worsening acne, easy bruising, facial or neck swelling, extreme fatigue, muscle weakness, irregular menstruation, hives, rash, itching, swelling of the face or extremities, hoarseness, difficulty breathing or swallowing, and wheezing. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms. Ciclesonide may slow growth in children, but it is unclear if it affects final adult height. Discuss the risks with your doctor before giving this medication to a child. Report any unusual problems while using this medication to your doctor. Store ciclesonide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture, and do not freeze it. Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose or accidental ingestion, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Prolonged overuse of ciclesonide may cause symptoms such as facial or neck swelling, worsening acne, easy bruising, extreme fatigue, muscle weakness, or irregular menstrual periods. Keep all appointments with your doctor. If the applicator becomes clogged, remove the dust cap, clean it with warm water, dry it, and replace it. Do not use sharp objects to clear the spray hole. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist with any questions about refilling your prescription.
